user.title: Connect Tick
user.description: Connect Home Assistant to your Tick. In Tick: Settings → Advanced → Keys → New key, access "Full access", named for example "Home Assistant". Paste that key here. Revoking the key in Tick disconnects Home Assistant at once.

data_description.api_key: Starts with tick_. Tick shows it only once.

reauth_confirm.title: New key for Tick
reauth_confirm.description: Tick no longer accepts the key for {url}. Make a new one in Tick (Settings → Advanced → Keys) and paste it here.

error.invalid_auth: Tick does not accept this key. Check that it is a key with full access and that it was not revoked.
error.not_enabled: This Tick does not have Home Assistant triggers switched on yet.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Tick at this address.

user.title: Add trigger
user.description: A trigger is a moment you can pick for a task in Tick, like "Sam comes home" or "The sun sets". Give it a name as you want to read it in Tick, then choose what Home Assistant watches. Leave the entity empty for a trigger that only goes off from its button or your own automation.

data_description.name: Short and clear: who or what, and what happens. For example "Sam comes home", "Sunset", "Bathroom light on".
data_description.entity_id: A person, the sun, a light, a door sensor… Optional.

state.title: When does "{name}" go off?
state.description: Choose the state {entity} has to change to. Tick is told the moment it changes to this state.

reconfigure.title: Change trigger
reconfigure.description: Tasks in Tick keep this trigger, also with a new name.

data_description.name: Short and clear: who or what, and what happens.
data_description.entity_id: Leave empty for a trigger that only goes off from its button or your own automation.

reconfigure_state.title: When does "{name}" go off?
reconfigure_state.description: Choose the state {entity} has to change to.

error.name_length: Give a name of 1 to 60 characters.
error.name_taken: There is already a trigger with this name.
